answer: In DeepWalk-style modeling, non-random walks are used as the node-sequence generator in place of ordinary unbiased random walks. They can be designed to follow specific rules or external signals—such as node attributes, edge weights, timestamps, labels, or other domain constraints—so the resulting sequences are then fed into the same skip-gram/word2vec-style objective to learn embeddings. Compared with using only ordinary graph structure, these walks can capture additional information beyond connectivity, such as semantic, temporal, weighted, or attribute-based relationships between nodes.
confidence_reasoning: This is a well-established extension of DeepWalk, though the exact kinds of non-random walks vary by method and application.
